correctness.rationale: PASS: A c.e. width-one prefix-closed tree with an infinite path has exactly one enumerated string at every level; waiting for its length-(n+1) string computes each path bit uniformly. For width two, Kleene recursion theorem supplies a self-referential enumerator. Each fresh split occurs above all previously enumerated levels; while a candidate output is awaited one provisional branch grows; after output b, only the opposite (1-b) side continues. At every time width<=2 and the resulting tree has a unique infinite path even if some simulated computation does not terminate. If the putative selector is total on promised inputs, infinitely many split coordinates violate eventual agreement. No finite enumeration is mistaken for a computability-theoretic proof.
